term: God (nominal definition of ST I q.13 a.8 ad 2)
definition: What the name 'God' is imposed to signify: something existing above all, which is the principle of all and remote from all (supra omnia existens, quod est principium omnium, et remotum ab omnibus). A nominal definition: what the name signifies, not what God is. Kept whole, with all three conditions. The fuller nominal premise STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-FULLY-DESCRIBED-PRINCIPLE formalizes it, together with the quarta via's 'cause of every perfection', reading 'remote from all' as DEF-REMOTE-FROM-ALL.
note: NominalGod is the antecedent of GodNamesTheFullyDescribedPrinciple as a predicate (maximal in being and the only such, causing the being and every perfection of every other being, remote from all): GOD_1 of the DISAMB-GOD fork (batch 4 of #1233). In this sense the naming premise and its converse are analytic (NOMINAL-GOD-NAMING-IS-ANALYTIC, NOMINAL-GOD-MAXIMALITY-IS-ANALYTIC); the root premise reads God as DEF-GOD-OF-CLASSICAL-THEISM.
